name: open-knowledge
title: inkeep/open-knowledge
description: OpenKnowledge: a markdown knowledge base for wikis, specs and notes, kept in notes/ and edited in its own tab beside the agent. Node and OpenKnowledge come installed, and the project starts OpenKnowledge by itself.
greeting:
OpenKnowledge — a markdown knowledge base for LLM wikis, specs and notes.

OpenKnowledge starts by itself: open this project's OpenKnowledge tab. The
knowledge base lives in /workspace/notes; keep every note there.

If the tab does not come up:
  cat /workspace/.rs-web.log      OpenKnowledge's own output (its last start)
  rs-web-restart                  restart OpenKnowledge
Turning the editor on or off rebuilds the project, which then reinstalls
OpenKnowledge first (about a minute). If that install does not finish, stop
the project and start it again.

To work with the agent, start it from the notes folder, in a second window
(F2):  cd /workspace/notes && claude
Log in first (/login): the project starts without credentials. Starting claude
in notes/ is what gives it OpenKnowledge's tools.

web.label: OpenKnowledge
web.start:
cd /workspace/notes || { echo "OpenKnowledge cannot start: /workspace/notes is missing."; exit 1; }
H="$HOME/.rs-history-status"; S=$(cat "$H" 2>/dev/null)
# A box keeping history waits while its notes may not be a clone of the notes
# repo yet: ok init in a plain folder would make it its own repository, and
# history could never attach to it afterwards.
if [ -e "$H" ] && [ "$S" != on ] && [ "$S" != off:push-failed ]; then
  echo "OpenKnowledge is waiting for its Gitea history ($S); see the terminal greeting."; exit 1
fi
# Once per container filesystem: ok init also registers OpenKnowledge for the
# agent in this box's home, which a fresh restart wipes.
if [ ! -e "$HOME/.rs-ok-init-done" ]; then
  ok init </dev/null || { echo "ok init failed (output above)."; exit 1; }
  touch "$HOME/.rs-ok-init-done"
fi
# With history on, turn on pull-and-push sync once; a setting changed later in
# OpenKnowledge is kept.
if [ "$S" = on ] && [ ! -e .ok/local/config.yml ]; then
  { mkdir -p .ok/local && t=$(mktemp .ok/local/.config.XXXXXX) && printf 'autoSync:\n  mode: full\n' > "$t" && mv -T "$t" .ok/local/config.yml; } || echo "could not turn on sync; turn it on in OpenKnowledge's settings."
fi
# A server lock left by an earlier container (a rebuild keeps notes/ and the
# hostname) can name a pid that is now another process, and OpenKnowledge
# then refuses to start. This script runs only while no app of the loop's
# runs, so a lock whose pid is not a running OpenKnowledge is stale.
L=.ok/local/server.lock
if [ -f "$L" ]; then
  p=$(sed -n 's/.*"pid": *\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p' "$L" | head -n 1)
  case "$(cat "/proc/${p:-0}/comm" 2>/dev/null)" in open-knowledge*) ;; *) rm -f -- "$L" ;; esac
fi
OK_ALLOW_EXTERNAL=1 exec ok start -p "$RS_BOX_WEB_PORT" --no-open-browser --idle-shutdown off --external-url "$RS_WEB_ADDRESS"
